YARA Rule Files
Create, edit, and delete rule files on disk. Rules are validated before saving and the hash cache is cleared automatically.
YARA Engine Settings
Configure regex timeout, concurrency limits, and failure posture. Secure defaults are fail-closed - alert-only modes require explicit admin consent.
Warning: fail_open_with_alert allows unscanned content to pass through when the engine is under stress. This weakens Zero Trust posture. Ensure alerting is operational before using this mode.
Full Content Scan Exclusions (ClamAV + YARA)

DIRECT Bypass Inventory

Every PAC path that returns DIRECT - a full security-path bypass: matching traffic skips SSL inspection, content scanning (ClamAV/YARA/DPI), CDR, Blocklist/URL Category enforcement, Threat Feed, authentication, policy, and all proxy logging - it never reaches Culvert. (This is not the same as an SSL-inspection bypass.) Derived from configuration: it shows what the config makes reachable, not that a bypass was used - Culvert cannot observe DIRECT traffic.

Change preview - what a config change would add, remove, or broaden

Enable only when running behind a trusted reverse proxy. When disabled, X-Forwarded-Host/Proto headers are ignored.

Reverse proxies whose X-Forwarded-For is trusted to resolve the real client IP for login lockout, admin-API rate limiting, the admin-IP allowlist, and audit attribution. 2-letter ISO code · Enter or comma to add · Backspace to remove last

A Decryption Profile controls how this tunnel is decrypted - including Inspect as HTTP/2, which removes the HTTP/1.1-downgrade anti-bot signal. Note: it does not change the TLS fingerprint (Culvert re-originates TLS with Go's stack), so destinations that fingerprint the ClientHello (JA3/JA4) or key on egress-IP reputation - e.g. Google - may still challenge; those need a Bypass rule or a warmed dedicated egress. Manage profiles under Decryption Profiles.

Evaluation order: Blocklist (hard block) → Threat Feeds → Policy Rules (below) → Default Action First matching policy rule wins. Blocklist and threat feed blocks happen before policy evaluation.

# Name Source Destination Country File Profile SSL Action Hits · total
∞ Default Drop (system) Matches all unmatched traffic - always last
Stage-1 outcome ≠ Allow. Auth Policy rules decide how a client authenticates - they never allow traffic. Stage-2 policy still decides access and default-deny still applies. Creating, editing, deleting and reordering these rules requires the admin role.
  • Exempt - skips end-user authentication only, and only when the client presents no credentials. No identity is ever created. Stage-2 still decides.
  • CredentialRequired - returns a deterministic 407 credential challenge; the client must authenticate first. It does not allow traffic, and the Stage-2 decision applies only after the client authenticates.
  • SSORequired - requires an interactive browser SSO login first: a browser is redirected (302) to the IdP, while a non-browser or CONNECT client is failed closed (403). It does not allow traffic; Stage-2 still decides access only after an identity exists.
Unsatisfiable or conflicting rules (no IdP, unavailable providerRefs, non-browser SSO, shadowed rules) are reported under Diagnostics.
The default policy action is Allow while auth rules exist - exemptions add little over an allow-all default. Set the default action to deny (Zero Trust).

Decryption Profiles

A Decryption Profile is the "how to decrypt" object a policy rule references (the rule's match criteria are the "what"). It controls Inspect as HTTP/2 (removes the HTTP/1.1-downgrade anti-bot signal), upstream certificate verification, the TLS version floor/cap, and the per-stream stall bound.
Honest scope: native HTTP/2 does not change the TLS fingerprint - Google-class destinations that fingerprint the ClientHello or key on egress-IP reputation may still challenge; those need a Bypass rule or warmed dedicated egress. Best fit: business-critical H2 SaaS you must keep inspected.

TLS parameter negotiation only (version/cipher below floor).
Whole inspect-failure class (can't-decrypt / client cert / pinning). Drives auto-exclusion.

Fail-open disables SSL inspection for hosts it can't decrypt. After a confirm-count of distinct clients, an incompatible host is auto-excluded and later sessions bypass inspection until it expires (12h; 1h pinned). Untrusted/expired certs are never excluded - they stay blocked. Learning is scoped to this profile only.

How auto-exclusion works
Learns on a genuine can't-decrypt signal only - the origin requires a client certificate, an unsupported TLS version, or a pinned client rejects our forged cert; generic origin errors and cert-validation failures do not qualify (they stay a 502 / block). Only the client-cert-required case rescues the current session; everything else is learn-only, so the first connection to a never-before-seen incompatible host still fails and the next self-heals - add known pinned apps to the manual SSL Bypass list for guaranteed first-session success. The cache is volatile and per-node. Every learn is alerted, audited, and listed under Decryption Exclusions. Keep inspection-mandatory hosts on fail-close rules - those are never learned or bypassed.
Policy Learning

Policy Learning is advisory only - it observes traffic and proposes born-disabled Allow rules with their evidence; it cannot alter enforcement policy. Scope is node-local: sessions, evidence, and recommendations are collected on this node only and are never aggregated across the fleet. Enabling the feature does not start observation - observation runs only while a Learning session you explicitly start is active. Identities are pseudonymized before anything is stored.

Loading…
Learning Sessions

Retained sessions on this node. Generate recommendations from a completed session; observation loss, category churn, and restart gaps are shown as operational facts.

-

Recommendations (advisory)

Each recommendation proposes ONE born-disabled Allow + Inspect rule for an observed group x category pair, with its evidence copied at generation time. Confidence (named predicates) and Coverage (facts about what was observed) are separate; membership percentages are never computed - the membership denominator unavailable state is shown instead. Staleness is computed by the server against the current policy, category, guardrail, and decision-policy identities. Accepting a recommendation (admin) creates a disabled rule in the Policy Draft candidate - it does not change enforcement until the draft is reviewed and committed.

-

Recommendable Categories (guardrail)

Fail-closed allowlist: only these exact category names may ever be recommended (empty = nothing recommendable). Seeded from the embedded business-category set until governed here. Changing the list changes the guardrail identity, so existing recommendations surface as stale; the change is refused while a Learning session is active.

Decryption Exclusions

These are hosts SSL inspection is currently OFF for - learned automatically because an inspected tunnel could not be established (unsupported TLS, the origin required a client certificate, or a pinned client rejected our certificate) under a rule whose Decryption Profile opts into fail-open. A host is only excluded after a confirm-count of distinct clients, and entries expire (12h; 1h for pinned). Each exclusion is scoped to the decryption profile that learned it - a host excluded under one profile is still inspected for rules using a different profile. An untrusted/expired origin certificate is never auto-excluded - that stays a block. This cache is volatile (cleared on restart, never synced between nodes) and is not part of config export/rollback. Every entry below means inspection coverage is reduced; evict any you don't expect.

Cache Tuning

These five parameters govern how the fail-open learn cache behaves on this node. Unlike the learned entries above (which are volatile and node-local), the parameters are durable - they survive restart. Changing a value applies immediately and does not wipe the current entries; new values take effect for future promotions. Tunables are node-local - set them on each node - and are deliberately not part of config export, versioned rollback, or cluster sync. The current effective values are the status line above (the single source of truth); the fields below are pre-filled from it.

Decryption Coverage

How much of this node's TLS is actually being inspected right now, and why the rest is not. Coverage is inspected ÷ (inspected + bypass/exclusion) - decryption failures are counted separately (they are sessions to triage, not a deliberate coverage gap). Counts are per-process since start; click any outcome or failure to see those sessions in the Live Feed.

Inspection-Coverage Trend

Per-interval inspection coverage over the recent window — is coverage eroding? Sampled once a minute; each point is that minute's inspected ÷ (inspected + bypass/exclusion). Volatile (resets on restart).

What is breaking decryption and where in the handshake (PAN-OS Decryption Error-Index parity).

Privacy

When on, the destination is pseudonymized with a keyed HMAC across every sink — the top-level host and uri, the nested dec.host / dec.sni, the request feed, the JSONL/history logs, the SIEM/syslog export, and the dashboard drill-down — so no plaintext destination is recorded. The token is stable, so a SOC can still correlate on it. The key is generated on first enable, node-local, and never exported/rolled-back/synced. Off by default.

Fail-closed: a node with the posture on but no key emits a constant redacted sentinel, never plaintext. Rotating or clearing the key breaks correlation with older records. Fleet-wide (cross-node) pseudonym correlation via a synced key is a separate follow-up.

MCP Command Center

MCP gateway posture: one place to decide if you need to act. All values below come from live /api/mcp/* responses.

MCP Servers & Tools

Read-only inventory for one tenant. Only safe identity and lifecycle fields are shown; raw endpoints, pinned identity material, credentials, and full tool schemas are never exposed. There are no inventory mutation actions in V1.

MCP Activity

Activity as a story: a Shadow-executed policy DENY is shown as DENY to executed (shadow) and can never read as a plain ALLOW. Select a row to open the evidence drawer.

MCP Policy & Simulator

A staged candidate workflow: review the active policy summary, draft a candidate, validate it, simulate a bounded test corpus, compare it against the active policy, and (Gateway only) create a publication request. A candidate is never active, validation is never publication, and a publication request is never approved or published.

MCP Approvals

One list for operational and publication approvals. Each item keeps its real kind and state. Decisions are four-eyes (a requester may not approve their own request) and require durable event storage; publication of an approved candidate is a separate step from approving it.

MCP Health & Durability

Gateway and Management runtime and durability are capability-isolated and shown independently. Detailed fleet acknowledgement lives on the Rollout & Fleet screen; this view links to it rather than duplicating it.

Management MCP Access

Management MCP is non-mutating in V1. This is an access and capability inventory, not an MCP client console: there are no tool-invocation, mutation, publication, or activation controls.

MCP Listener Settings

Gateway and Management are separate and default disabled. Storing configuration is node-local only: it does NOT bind, activate, or restart a live listener, and it never distributes CP to DP. Management mutation stays disabled in V1 and cannot be enabled here. No wildcard bind and no shared endpoint; the appliance validates and replaces the complete configuration atomically.

Enroll new Sluice instance
CDR is currently disabled.
Enrolling your first Sluice instance will also turn CDR on automatically - you don't need to touch the config file or restart the proxy. The choice persists across restarts (stored at /data/cdr_enabled).

The token + fingerprint pair come from the Sluice admin. Fingerprint is TOFU-pinned - a mismatch rejects the handshake even with a valid token. On success Culvert stores the mTLS bundle at /data/integrations/sluice/<name>/ (0600). Get the fingerprint over a trusted channel (the same SSH session that ran docker exec ... sluice token, not a paste from chat) - an attacker who can substitute the fingerprint alongside a valid token gets a rogue enrollment.

Cert lifecycle (Sluice v0.1)
Client certs are valid for 1 year. When they expire, Sluice v0.1 has no renewal RPC - operators must Revoke this instance and re-enroll with a fresh token + fingerprint. Sluice v0.2 will add RenewCert for zero-touch renewal.
If the server cert on Sluice is regenerated, the TOFU pin breaks and re-enrollment is required - plan server-side rotations during a maintenance window or wait for Sluice v0.2's dual-pin grace window.

-
Fencing Lease
-
Sync to Leader

Fencing is configured at startup (--ha-etcd-endpoints / cluster.etcd_endpoints) and read once - this panel shows status only. With a lease armed, leadership and automatic failover are arbitrated by etcd; write authority requires a live lease. The Term tile above equals the epoch of the currently-held fencing lease (ADR-0005: term = a held lease's epoch). In a failure state where no lease is held - e.g. a leader that restarted and cannot reacquire the etcd lease, running read-only - the lease card shows epoch 0 while Term retains the last synced value, so the two can differ precisely when you are diagnosing a fencing problem.

This standby polls the leader every ~5s. The Sync to Leader tile shows the current consecutive-failure streak - it resets to 0 on every successful sync. At the configured threshold this standby stops waiting and either self-promotes (automatic failover / fencing lease) or, if automatic failover is off, stays read-only until an operator promotes it manually. Watching this tile climb is your early warning before that happens.

Use when the leader is down and automatic failover is off. Confirm the leader is truly gone first - promoting while the leader still serves causes split-brain.
Recent role transitions
WhenFromToEpochReason

In-memory history (cleared on restart); raw local facts, not a cluster-wide failover analysis.

          Support
          

            
            
            
            
            
            
            
          

        

        

          
Diagnostic support bundles are redacted at source - secrets are dropped and identifiers masked before anything is written. Creating a bundle is admin-only; a standard bundle may contain internal (non-secret) operational detail.


          

            
Health verdict

            
Loading…

          


          

            

              Backups
              
            

            
Archive directory scanned by the maintenance agent - the same listing --list-backups produces, without SSH.

            
Loading…

          


          

            
Capture level

            
Elevate the default bundle capture depth for a bounded window. A TTL is mandatory - the level auto-reverts to baseline when it expires (even across a restart).

            
Loading…

            
            

              
              
              
              
              
              
            

          


          

            
Retention tuning

            
Node-local caps on the persisted bundle store. Case-bound (evidence) bundles are exempt from every cap; pending (unapproved) bundles are exempt from the count cap only, so a tightened age cap can still age one out. A 2 GiB store ceiling is always active. Tightening a cap is a one-way door — evicted bundles cannot be recovered, and a change that would evict bundles must be confirmed.

            
Loading…

            

              
              
              
              
              
            

          


          

            
Diagnostics

            
Local, read-only checks - no network, no shell.

            

              
              
              
              
              
              
              
              
              
              
              
            

            

          


          

            
Sealing recipients (manual export only)

            
Register a public X25519 key once (verify its fingerprint out-of-band), then seal a manually-downloaded bundle to it by name - no pasting raw keys. Keys are validated on registration; nothing here is secret. This registry is separate from the "TAC trust keys" below - it feeds only the manual Seal download, not the automated Upload to TAC button, which reads its recipient key from TAC trust keys instead.

            

              
              
              
            

            
Loading…

          


          

            
TAC secure upload

            
Optional outbound upload of a bundle to a TAC portal. Off by default and never automatic - a bundle only leaves on an explicit, per-bundle, case-bound admin action (the Upload to TAC button on a ready bundle below). The bundle is sealed end-to-end to TAC's public key before it leaves. Set the TAC origin (https; a private/internal address is refused - use offline export for air-gapped transfer) and enable it here to make upload available.

            
Loading…

            

              
              
              
              
              
            

            
TAC trust keys

            
The public recipient key(s) a bundle is sealed to. Verify a key's fingerprint against TAC's published value out-of-band. Read-only (baked into the build or set via CULVERT_TAC_TRUST_KEYS).

            
Loading…

            
Upload queue

            
Loading…

          


          

            
Telemetry (opt-in)

            
Off by default. When enabled, a small set of the appliance's own support-health scalars (see the preview below - review it first) would be periodically sealed end-to-end and sent to TAC over authenticated HTTPS: never traffic volume, customer scale, or security-posture data. This build performs no network transmission of any kind - there is no sender yet, so enabling here only stores this configuration locally. Telemetry consent is entirely separate from the support-bundle upload consent above - enabling one never enables the other. This whole section is admin-only.
